# automox_policy (Resource)

An Automox policy: a patch policy, a worklet, or a required-software deployment, run on a schedule against the devices in its server groups.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A patch policy. Schedules can be written in plain terms rather than as the
# encoded integer Automox stores.

resource "automox_policy" "monthly_patching" {
  name          = "Monthly Patching"
  policy_type   = "patch"
  notes         = "Managed by Terraform"
  server_groups = [automox_server_group.workstations.id]

  schedule_time         = "03:00"
  schedule_days_of_week = ["saturday"]

  configuration = {
    patch_rule = "all"

    # Automox requires filter_type on every patch policy, not only when
    # patch_rule is "filter".
    filter_type = "include"
    filters     = []

    auto_patch  = true
    auto_reboot = false
    notify_user = true
  }
}

# A worklet. Automox calls this policy type "custom"; "worklet" is rejected.
resource "automox_policy" "disk_space_check" {
  name          = "Report Low Disk Space"
  policy_type   = "custom"
  server_groups = [automox_server_group.workstations.id]

  schedule_time         = "06:00"
  schedule_days_of_week = ["monday"]

  configuration = {
    # Required for worklets, and matched exactly: "windows" is rejected.
    os_family = "Windows"

    evaluation_code = <<-EOT
      $free = (Get-PSDrive C).Free / 1GB
      if ($free -lt 10) { exit 0 } else { exit 1 }
    EOT

    remediation_code = <<-EOT
      Write-Output "Low disk space on $env:COMPUTERNAME"
    EOT

    auto_reboot = false
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `configuration` (Attributes) Policy behaviour. Which attributes apply depends on `policy_type` and, for patch policies, on `patch_rule`; the provider validates the combination before calling the API. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration))
- `name` (String) Policy name. **Must be unique within the organization.** Automox returns no identifier when a policy is created, so the provider finds the new policy by name; a duplicate name makes that lookup ambiguous and the apply fails rather than guessing.
- `notes` (String) Free-text notes. Automox requires this even though it is descriptive.
- `policy_type` (String) One of `patch`, `custom` (a worklet), or `required_software`. Changing this replaces the policy.
- `schedule_time` (String) Time of day the policy runs, as `HH:MM` on a 24-hour clock. Interpreted in each device's local time unless `use_scheduled_timezone` is set.
- `server_groups` (List of Number) IDs of the server groups this policy targets.

### Optional

- `schedule_days` (Number) Days of the week the policy runs, as Automox's encoded bitmask. Prefer `schedule_days_of_week`, which is readable; this is set automatically from it. `0` means the policy never runs on a day-of-week schedule.

The encoding is 1-indexed with bit 0 unused: bit 1 is Monday through bit 7 Sunday, so `254` is every day.
- `schedule_days_of_week` (Set of String) Days of the week the policy runs, for example `["monday", "thursday"]`. Conflicts with `schedule_days`, which is the encoded form of the same thing.
- `schedule_months` (Number) Months the policy runs, as Automox's encoded bitmask. Prefer `schedule_months_of_year`.
- `schedule_months_of_year` (Set of String) Months the policy runs, for example `["march", "september"]`. Conflicts with `schedule_months`.
- `schedule_weeks_of_month` (Number) Weeks of the month the policy runs, as Automox's encoded bitmask, where `62` is every week.

There is no named equivalent for this field. The bit order is believed to be 1-indexed from the first week, but one live policy contradicts that and the cause is unresolved, so the provider does not offer a friendly form it cannot guarantee. A wrong week order would silently move when patching runs.
- `scheduled_timezone` (String) UTC offset used when `use_scheduled_timezone` is true, in Automox's `UTC+0000` form — not an IANA zone name.
- `use_scheduled_timezone` (Boolean) When true, `schedule_time` is interpreted in `scheduled_timezone` rather than in each device's local time.

### Read-Only

- `create_time` (String)
- `id` (Number) Policy ID.
- `next_remediation` (String) When Automox expects to run this policy next. Null when the schedule means it will never run.
- `organization_id` (Number)
- `server_count` (Number) Devices this policy currently applies to.
- `status` (String) `active` or `inactive`.
- `uuid` (String) Policy UUID. Automox does not return one for `required_software` policies, where this stays null.

<a id="nestedatt--configuration"></a>
### Nested Schema for `configuration`

Optional:

- `advanced_filter` (Attributes List) Filter expressions for `patch_rule = "advanced"`. Automox requires at least one when that rule is selected. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration--advanced_filter))
- `auto_patch` (Boolean) Install patches automatically when the policy runs.
- `auto_reboot` (Boolean) Reboot devices automatically after patching.
- `custom_notification_deferment_periods` (List of Number) Deferral options offered to the user, in hours. At most three, each 24 or fewer.
- `custom_notification_max_delays` (Number)
- `custom_notification_patch_message` (String) Windows patch notification text, up to 125 characters.
- `custom_notification_patch_message_mac` (String) macOS patch notification text, up to 70 characters.
- `custom_notification_reboot_message` (String)
- `custom_notification_reboot_message_mac` (String)
- `custom_pending_reboot_notification_deferment_periods` (List of Number)
- `custom_pending_reboot_notification_max_delays` (Number)
- `custom_pending_reboot_notification_message` (String)
- `custom_pending_reboot_notification_message_mac` (String)
- `device_filters` (Attributes List) Narrows the policy to a subset of the devices in its server groups. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration--device_filters))
- `device_filters_enabled` (Boolean)
- `evaluation_code` (String) Script deciding whether remediation is needed. Despite the vendor documentation, the API returns this on patch policies as well.
- `filter_type` (String) `include`, `exclude`, or `severity`.

Automox requires this on **every** patch policy, not only when `patch_rule = "filter"` as its error message suggests.
- `filters` (List of String) Package names to include or exclude, used with `filter_type`.
- `include_optional` (Boolean) Include optional Windows updates.
- `install_deferral_enabled` (Boolean)
- `install_do_not_disturb_honored` (Boolean)
- `install_notification_deadline` (Number) Hours before installation is forced. Not present in Automox's published schema, but returned by the API.
- `installation_code` (String) Installation script. Required for `required_software` policies.
- `is_patch_tuesday` (Boolean) Run only on the second Tuesday of the month.
- `missed_patch_window` (Boolean)
- `notify_deferred_reboot_user` (Boolean)
- `notify_deferred_reboot_user_auto_deferral_enabled` (Boolean)
- `notify_deferred_reboot_user_message_timeout` (Number)
- `notify_reboot_user` (Boolean)
- `notify_user` (Boolean)
- `notify_user_auto_deferral_enabled` (Boolean)
- `notify_user_message_timeout` (Number) Minutes a notification stays up, 15 to 480.
- `os_family` (String) `Windows`, `Mac`, or `Linux`. Required for worklet and required-software policies.

Matched exactly: `macOS` and lowercase `windows` are both rejected.
- `package_name` (String)
- `package_version` (String)
- `patch_rule` (String) How a patch policy selects patches: `all`, `filter`, `manual`, or `advanced`. Patch policies only.
- `patch_tuesday_offset` (Number) Days after Patch Tuesday to run, 0 to 26.
- `pending_reboot_deferral_enabled` (Boolean)
- `pending_reboot_notification_deadline` (Number) Hours before a pending reboot is forced. Not present in Automox's published schema, but returned by the API.
- `reboot_do_not_disturb_honored` (Boolean)
- `refresh_before_remediation` (Boolean)
- `remediation_code` (String) Script run when evaluation indicates remediation is needed.
- `severity_filter` (List of String) Severities to act on when `filter_type = "severity"`: `no_known_cves`, `none`, `unknown`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `critical`.

<a id="nestedatt--configuration--advanced_filter"></a>
### Nested Schema for `configuration.advanced_filter`

Required:

- `left` (String) Field to filter on: `display-name`, `severity`, `patch-source`, `patch-os`, `type`, or `patch-days-old`.
- `right` (String)

Optional:

- `op` (String)


<a id="nestedatt--configuration--device_filters"></a>
### Nested Schema for `configuration.device_filters`

Required:

- `field` (String) `tag`, `hostname`, `ip_addr`, `os_family`, `os_version_id`, or `organizational_unit`.
- `op` (String) `in` (is), `not_in` (is not), `like_any` (contains), or `not_like_any` (does not contain).
- `value` (List of String)

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Policies import by their integer ID.
terraform import automox_policy.monthly_patching 824368
```
